item.title: Naramachi: The Old Merchant Quarter — Guide
item.description: Naramachi, spreading south from Sarusawa Pond and Kofukuji, is the former merchant district of Nara, a well-preserved warren of narrow lanes lined with traditional machiya townhouses — deep, wooden merchant homes with latticed facades that grew up in the grounds of the vanished Gangoji temple. Today the quarter is one of Nara’s most enjoyable strolls, its historic buildings converted into stylish cafes, craft boutiques, sake shops, galleries and small museums, including a restored machiya open to visitors and a shop of the red ‘migawari-zaru’ good-luck monkey charms that hang from the eaves throughout the district.

item.title: Takayama Sanmachi Suji: A Beautifully Preserved Merchant Old Town — Guide
item.description: Sanmachi Suji is the beautifully preserved heart of Takayama’s old town, a cluster of narrow lanes lined with dark wooden merchant houses dating from the Edo period, when the town prospered as a centre of skilled carpenters and merchants in the mountainous Hida region. Today the lanes are home to sake breweries marked by cedar-ball signs, cafes, craft shops, and stalls selling Hida beef and local sweets, making it one of Japan’s most atmospheric and enjoyable historic districts to explore on foot.

item.title: Chichibu Shrine & Old Town: A Mountain-Ringed Sacred Centre — Guide
item.description: Chichibu Shrine, with a history stretching back some 2,100 years, is one of the oldest and most revered shrines in the Kanto region, its vividly carved wooden gate and main hall set against the dramatic backdrop of the Chichibu mountains. The surrounding old town retains a quaint, small-city charm with traditional shops and eateries, serving as the spiritual and social heart of an area famous nationwide for its elaborate December night festival, one of Japan’s three great float festivals.
